One of the biggest hurdles I hear from people is the financial one. I don't think I have ever heard anyone say they failed because of bad time management even though they had decent cash flow. Self-discipline is huge and in my mind related to income sources.

Which is what I would recommend figuring out first. You need to know how much you want to make and how much is the bare minimum you can survive on. When I say "survive", that means you have to be putting money away into savings and retirement. You are not doing yourself any good by ignoring that.

To figure out how much you need, base it off your current pay. Look at your gross pay per check/cheque, figure out the percentage of it that goes to taxes, insurance, 401k, etc that you may have on there. Now you know part of the equation. Next, you need to list off expenses related to running your business. Are you going to need stationary (business cards, uniforms, paper receipt/invoices)? What equipment do you need (computer/laptop, tablet, phone, point-of-sale register)? How are you going to deal with your web presence (website, custom email domain, social media accounts)? How much does it cost for you to register your business with your state? You also need to check with the county and city to see if they require additional registration forms and fees.

So now you have some idea of what you need to figure out how much you need to be earning per week/month in order to be successful. Let's say, for the sake of rounding things off to be easy, you want to gross $60,000 per year. Your taxes total up to 10%, your insurance costs an additional 20%, retirement is 5%, and your monthly running cost will be $300 (5%), you want to put 10% into savings, and now you are at $30,000 left over. Is that enough to cover mortgage/rent, food, gas for the car, utilities, cell phone(s), and all your other expenses? Look over the last 4 to 6 months of your bank statements, see how much you are averaging in all those categories.

Since you know you want to make $5,000 per month, and for the sake of the thought experiment you don't want to work more than 40 hours per week, you now know you have to average $31.25 per hour.

That gives you a starting point to figure out your finances. But there is something else I would stress at this point, your branding. It can be more of an impact than you may initially think. When you have an idea for a name, check if the .com is available. Check if social media handles are taken (such as on Twitter/Facebook/etc). Try not to get something that is too odd but still not completely saturated when you reach online for it.

Anyway, just my two cents.
